isolated_readonly_results.limits: Temporary SQLite reproduction does not exclude every possible checkpoint or filesystem wait. Four-thread function replay does not reproduce the complete live process workload.

native_sample.claim: Observed GIL contention and large-object churn, not a traced SQLite busy wait; exact complete latency cause remains unproven.

reproduced_frontend_defect.test_method: Exact current JS executed in HappyDOM with a controlled held fetch; no live requests sent.
reproduced_frontend_defect.implication: Slow requests permit overlapping dashboard rebuilds and response-body allocations. This can amplify load; it is not alone proof of the whole 65-second delay.

minimal_candidate_repair.action: Coalesce load() calls: at most one dashboard request in flight and one trailing refresh when a newer trigger arrived. Preserve original request-order and placementEpoch reconciliation. Coalesce repeated timer/SSE events without unbounded queueing. A transport error must release the flight slot.
must_preserve: One-second local quote expiry and hiding expired instructions
Current server EvidenceGuard, readiness and numerical seal checks
A fresh follow-up request after checklist changes or new publication while a request is pending
No rewriting prior odds, stakes, losses or placement history
minimal_candidate_repair.acceptance: Prove with a controlled held response that repeated poll/SSE triggers never create parallel dashboard fetches, one follow-up obtains the newest state, errors permit retry, and existing stale-response/checklist/expiry DOM tests still pass. Then rerun the original D22 loaded HTTP acceptance; do not close D22 from this client-only fix.
